title: Telescan catalog entry
description: One application. Put one entry per file in data/apps.d/<id>.json.

$schema.description: A link to this file, so that an editor can complete and check the entry.

id.description: Short lowercase ID, and also the file name. Used on the command line.

name.description: The name the vendor uses, plus a version note when the entry is version specific.

platforms.description: The platforms the entry applies to.

what.description: What the application sends, in one or two sentences.

default_state.description: The state of a fresh install, used when no check finds anything.

docs.description: A link to the vendor documentation for the opt-out.

verification.description: How well the audit supports the checks. confirmed: vendor documentation or upstream source supports the control. qualified: the control is real, but its scope is narrower or some details are not verified. unresolved: the audit did not establish the control, so the entry can only use manual checks.

verified_at.description: The date of the last audit of this entry, as YYYY-MM-DD.

scope.description: The kinds of data collection that the checks cover. Other kinds are out of scope.

evidence.description: Primary evidence: links to vendor documentation or upstream source.

versions.description: The application versions the entry applies to, for example ">=2.1100.0" or ">=6,<7". Needs "version".

version_range.description: Comma separated clauses that must all hold, for example ">=6,<7".

version.description: How to read the installed version. Files are read first. The command only runs with --run-commands. The first dotted number in the value is the version.

files.description: JSON files that hold the version, in order of precedence.

key.description: files: the key that holds the version.

argv.description: A command that prints the version.

detect.description: How to tell that the application is installed. Give at least one of the two.

which.description: Executables to look for on PATH.

paths.description: Files or directories to look for. Placeholders and globs are allowed.

path.description: A path that may hold the placeholders {home}, {config}, {data}, {appsupport}, {appdata}, {localappdata} or {programdata}, and glob wildcards.

steps.description: What the user must do, one instruction per item.

commands.description: Commands that do the same thing, for a copy and paste.

env.description: Environment variables that turn the telemetry off.

match_list.description: Values to compare against. Use *truthy* or *falsy* for the usual words.

check.description: One place to read. The scanner reports the sum of all checks.

component.description: Independent control; every component must be off for the app to be OFF.

profiles.description: Read every matching file as a separate profile instead of using file precedence.

default_state.description: Fallback for this component or profile when its setting is absent.

key.description: json/ini: the setting name. In json a dot is a path separator.

section.description: ini: the section name. DEFAULT when absent.

files.description: The files to read, in order of precedence.

exact.description: env/json/ini: compare literal values as case sensitive strings. A JSON boolean does not match a string.

disabled_pattern.description: regex/command: a pattern that proves the telemetry is off.

enabled_pattern.description: regex/command: a pattern that proves the telemetry is on.

present.description: file: the state to report when the file exists.

argv.description: command: the command to run. Only runs with --allow-commands.

versions.description: The application versions this check applies to. Out of range, the check is skipped. When the version is unknown, the check cannot prove ON or OFF. Needs "version" on the entry.
